name: Armando
bio: A young Roman whom Wilde knew in April 1900, described to Robert Ross as 'a very smart elegant young Roman Sporus' and, at greater length, as being 'so absurdly like the Apollo Belvedere that I feel always as if I was Winckelmann when I am with him'. Wilde gave him up over the cost of his clothes, took up his best friend instead, and had forgiven him within a fortnight. He survives under a first name only.
bio_note: Added 2026-08-06. HE IS THE BEST-DOCUMENTED OF THE ROME COHORT: two folios, both read at the page, one of them carrying a sustained physical description of a kind Wilde wrote about almost nobody else this late. 'Sporus' was Nero's boy-favourite and is not an ambiguous word in Wilde's vocabulary; 'Winckelmann' is Johann Joachim Winckelmann, to whom Pater devoted a chapter of The Renaissance and whose name in this circle carries the whole freight of adult male desire for young men modelled on Greek sculpture. NOTHING SEXUAL IS STATED and none is claimed here. NO AGE IS GIVEN and none is inferred; the index calls him a boy, Wilde does not. THE TRANSACTIONAL SHAPE IS ON THE RECORD and is not smoothed over: 'his requests for raiment and neckties were incessant: he really bayed for boots'. THE ROME COHORT: Wilde was in Rome from about 12 April to early May 1900, seven months before his death, and wrote about it to Robert Ross. Three young Romans are named in those letters - Armando, Arnaldo and Omero. None of the three was on this map until 2026-08-06, although the map already carried the Naples, Napoule and Paris cohorts in detail. The gap existed because only Armando has his own General Index entry ('Armando (boy), 1182, 1184'); the other two appear inside the same paragraphs and are indexed nowhere. See [[arnaldo]] and [[omero]].
